findings.title: Undefined name in reservation check always raises
findings.issue: `_reservation_is_current` references `strict`, which is not a parameter or local, so any StorageError/ValueError/KeyError/TypeError in the check path becomes NameError instead of a bounded deny or ScopePreparationUnknown. Executable path: call `_reservation_is_current` on a reservation after inducing a policy storage error; the NameError escapes callers expecting CapabilityDenied/StorageError.
findings.fix: Add a `strict=False` parameter matching `_commit_durable_transport`, and raise ScopePreparationUnknown only when strict; otherwise return False.

findings.title: Scope allowlist can widen beyond SCOPES at token exchange
findings.issue: `callback` sends `'scope':' '.join(row['scopes'])` on the token request, and `_validate_bundle` then requires the returned scope set to be exactly within the requested scopes. However a malicious or compromised authorization server can return scopes the user never granted if they were in `SCOPES` but not in `row['scopes']` — no, actual<=set(scopes) blocks this. Real issue: `row['scopes']` is Jsonb(list(scopes)) and is later used to authorize refresh (`credential` line 185) with the same scope list, but `refresh` can return narrower or different scope; `_validate_bundle` requires exact set containment both directions except offline_access, so a provider that omits `offline_access` in refresh is fine but one that drops e.g. `Mail.Send` fails closed. The actual defect: `callback` uses `row['scopes']` from the DB row fetched before the loop, but `row` is a dict row of the `flows` table; if `scopes` was inserted as Jsonb, psycopg returns a Python list, so `' '.join(row['scopes'])` works, but `set(scopes)` at begin time permits any tuple ordering and duplicates; more critically `begin` does not bind the requested scopes to the connection's existing account scopes, so a second `begin` on the same connection_ref with different scopes is allowed and the account's scopes are silently replaced at callback (line 163-165) without the owner re-approving the scope change.
findings.fix: Reject scope-set changes on an existing connection unless a new connection_ref is used, or require explicit scope downgrade/upgrade confirmation bound to the exact prior revision.

findings.title: Calendar sync marks previously synced events deleted on partial scope change
findings.issue: On a complete sync, `UPDATE ... SET deleted=true ... WHERE payload->>'scope_digest'=%s AND NOT(id=ANY(%s))` is scoped by scope_digest, but `read_calendar` may be called with a narrower selection window that yields fewer events; since digest changes with selection, this is scoped correctly. However if the same digest is reused with a smaller `max_pages` in a prior partial run and later completes, events only reachable on later pages are preserved; but if the provider's page ordering changes and an event drops out of the first `max_pages`, the completion path still marks events not in `events` as deleted even if they were never re-observed because `complete=True` is only set when all pages were consumed. Real defect: `complete` can be True when `pages<max_pages` and cursor is None on the last page of the last calendar, yet the deletion sweep uses `events` accumulated across ALL calendars; if calendar A consumed all pages and calendar B had zero events, events from a prior run of the same digest that were on calendar A are retained, but events previously synced under the same digest from a calendar_ref that is no longer in selection.calendar_refs are silently marked deleted without a stale-scope warning.
findings.fix: Delete only within the currently selected calendar_refs (or record scope_digest per calendar_ref), and never mark deleted when selection coverage is partial or the selection payload changed.

findings.title: Token vault secret_ref deleted before older secret cleanup ordering
findings.issue: After committing the new secret, `if prior and prior['secret_ref']: self.vault.delete(prior['secret_ref'])` runs after the transaction commits but the exception handler at line 168 deletes `secret` if the commit raised; if the commit succeeded and then deletion of the obsolete secret fails (e.g. filesystem error), the obsolete secret remains on disk indefinitely. Additionally, if a concurrent credential() call read the old secret_ref between commit and delete, it may refresh using a stale refresh_token after the old secret is deleted, causing vault.get failures rather than a clean 'reconnect required'.
findings.fix: Delete the obsolete secret_ref inside the same transaction's callback or record it for cleanup after commit with a durable cleanup queue; make credential() treat missing secret_ref as 'interactive reconnect required' rather than StorageError.

findings.title: Action receipt unknown status not surfaced to caller as non-retryable
findings.issue: Any exception during execute is converted to ExecutionOutcome('unknown', error_code=type(error).__name__) and persisted, then the receipt is returned. Callers see a receipt with status 'unknown' but nothing in the runtime marks this as 'must not be blindly retried'; `ActionRuntime.confirm_and_execute` simply returns the receipt. A second call with the same proposal_ref/version returns `prior[-1]` (the unknown receipt) rather than raising, so a caller that inspects only `.status` may still trigger reconciliation/retry semantics incorrectly. Also `type(error).__name__` may leak exception class names into the durable receipt, which is minor privacy/robustness concern.
findings.fix: Return or raise a distinct non-retryable error alongside the unknown receipt, and normalize error_code to a bounded allowlist of identifiers.

findings.title: Mail body content returned to caller without per-call grant binding to read_message
findings.issue: `read_message` authorizes with resource_ref=message_ref and data_class='private_connector_content', but then calls `self.transport.request(decision,...)` which internally re-validates decision.owner_ref/connection_ref/provider_ref only. The returned dict includes full message body content and is returned to the caller; the `source_scope` field reconstructs an AuthorizationRequest with `replace(scope,operation_ref=None)` — but operation_ref=None means downstream require_authorized_operation consumers may treat this as a valid grant. Also no explicit check that message_ref corresponds to a message in the selected folder before authorization, only after the HTTP fetch; if a caller supplies an arbitrary message_ref the request is made before the scope check at line 241.
findings.fix: Validate message_ref against selection scope before issuing the HTTP request where possible, and never emit an AuthorizationRequest-shaped object with operation_ref=None in user-visible output; emit a plain provenance dict instead.

findings.title: Action preflight busy-check skips cancelled events but does not validate timezone change
findings.issue: `_preflight` parses start_at/end_at and validates end>start, but does not verify that content['timezone'] is the same timezone used in `_calendar_time` conversion or that the interval length is bounded. An arbitrarily large interval (e.g. 10 years) is accepted as long as free/busy returns no busy events; with $top=100 and @odata.nextLink check this is bounded but a very wide interval could still be a resource/budget concern.
findings.fix: Bound the proposed calendar interval length (e.g. max 30 days) and validate the timezone against an allowlist or known ZoneInfo at preview and edit time.

findings.title: Academic collect swallows exceptions as coverage without distinguishing denial vs transport
findings.issue: `except Exception: coverage.append(course+':'+surface+':unavailable'); break` treats CapabilityDenied and StorageError identically, so an authorization denial is recorded as 'unavailable' rather than 'scope_denied' and the collector does not surface that the source was never authorized. This can produce a report that appears to have checked coverage when the grant was missing.
findings.fix: Catch CapabilityDenied separately and record 'scope_denied'; reserve 'unavailable' for transport/storage errors.

findings.title: Vault put does not fsync parent directory after create
findings.issue: File contents are fsynced but the containing directory entry is not, so a crash immediately after put may lose the file while the DB secret_ref references it. This is a durability gap rather than a correctness bug in normal operation.
findings.fix: Open and fsync the vault directory after writing the sealed file.

not_verified: Actual Graph token endpoint behavior and scope echo.
Whether pa_actions attempts FK on confirmations prevents re-insertion races in all isolation levels.
Whether registry.execute_reserved re-checks current_transport_requests for background_metadata_read under all call paths.
Real Mail.ReadBasic vs Mail.Read scope enforcement at Microsoft Graph.
Whether TokenVault.delete failure paths are ever surfaced to the owner.
summary: The code is generally fail-closed with strong owner/scope/version binding, one-use OAuth state, and durable unknown-attempt fences. However there are two P0-level defects: an undefined name in `_reservation_is_current` that will raise NameError on any policy error path, and an unsafely scoped connection scope replacement that lets a second `begin` silently change the account's granted scopes without re-approval. Several P1 issues around exception swallowing in academic collection, unknown-action retry semantics, and calendar deletion scoping should be fixed before shipping.
